overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a marine-influenced morning with temperatures stuck at 66-67°F through 08:52, well below where models expect the daily high to land. The running max of 69.8°F was set around midnight (00:10 ET), roughly 9.6 hours ago, meaning the station has yet to surpass that mark despite slow warming underway. High dewpoint (62.6°F), patchy fog, and mostly cloudy skies reflect a strong marine layer that is suppressing early warming and will likely cap the afternoon high.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS (76.6°F), HRRR (76.4°F), and NWS (76°F) are tightly clustered, while ECMWF (75.0°F) is modestly cooler and NBM (71.3°F) is notably more conservative — likely weighting the persistent marine layer more heavily. The D1_NOW ensemble strongly favors 74-75°F (57.2%) with secondary weight at 72-73°F (42.4%), sitting below the NWS/GFS/HRRR consensus and aligning closest to ECMWF; the intraday model's elevated probabilities in the 80-84°F range appear driven by a transient velocity signal that has since stalled (30-min velocity = 0.0°F/hr, acceleration = -0.900°F/hr²) and should be discounted.
max_temp_prediction: With peak timing expected near 15:00-17:30 ET and the current temperature at 68°F, the atmosphere needs roughly 7-8°F of additional warming to reach NWS/GFS/HRRR guidance — achievable but contingent on cloud breaks that may not materialize given the Coastal Flood Advisory, Beach Hazards Statement, and possible afternoon showers (11am-5pm per NWS). The D1_NOW top even-bucket consensus of 74-75°F and ECMWF's 75.0°F forecast represent the most credible central estimate; the active even-bucket market's top bucket of 74-75°F at 57.2% looks well-supported. Confidence is moderate — a marine layer breakdown could push toward 76-77°F, but persistent clouds and shower activity keep downside risk to the 72-73°F range real.
